description: We are ORBIT NEXUS, a six-member team from Karachi joining the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. We aim to build astronaut health monitoring software that tracks key health indicators, spots concerning trends, and supports informed decisions during long space missions. Our interests include software development, AI, data visualization, human health, and space science. We focus on clear design, credible research, and practical solutions. Dream Bigger. Design Beyond.
summary:
ASTRA-HEALTH is an AI-assisted astronaut health monitoring and assessment platform designed to support crew health during long-duration space missions. It collects physiological, behavioral, and environmental indicators, including heart rate, body temperature, blood oxygen, sleep, stress, and cabin CO₂ levels.

The platform compares new measurements with an astronaut's personal baseline using rule-based assessment and machine learning anomaly detection to identify unusual changes and patterns. It presents understandable health insights, alerts, historical trends, and preventive guidance through an interactive dashboard and 2D human body map.

By helping astronauts understand what has changed and why it may need attention, ASTRA-HEALTH aims to support better-informed health decisions, especially when communication with Earth is delayed. It is a decision-support prototype, not a medical diagnosis system.
details:
Project Overview

ASTRA-HEALTH (Astronaut Health Assessment and Intelligence Platform) is an AI-assisted health monitoring prototype developed by Team ORBIT NEXUS for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

The platform is designed to help astronauts monitor physiological, behavioral, and environmental indicators during long-duration space missions. It collects measurements such as heart rate, blood pressure, body temperature, oxygen saturation, sleep duration, mood, stress, physical activity, and cabin CO₂ levels.

How It Works

The system validates incoming readings and stores them with timestamps and data-source information. It compares new measurements with an astronaut's personal historical baseline, applies rule-based assessment, and uses machine learning anomaly detection to identify unusual patterns.

The results are presented through a health dashboard, interactive 2D human body map, alerts, health insights, historical charts, and reports. The system aims to explain what has changed, why it may need attention, and what should be checked next.

Technology

The project uses a React-based web interface, Python and FastAPI for backend services, SQLite for data storage, and Python data-science libraries including Pandas, NumPy, and Scikit-learn for analysis and anomaly detection.

Data and Limitations

The prototype uses simulated astronaut measurements for demonstrations and NASA research resources for scientific context. Data sources are identified separately. Its outputs are intended for decision support and human review, not medical diagnosis. It is not a certified medical device, and its prototype thresholds and model results are not clinically validated.

Intended Impact

ASTRA-HEALTH explores how understandable health monitoring and onboard data analysis could support astronaut awareness and better-informed decisions when communication with Earth is delayed.
